sanskrit: pūrvajaṃ nakulety evaṃ sahadeveti cāparam mādrīputrāv akathayaṃs te viprāḥ prītamānasāḥ anusaṃvatsaraṃ jātā api te kurusattamāḥ
english: The Brahmins, with joyful hearts, named the elder of Mādrī's sons Nakula and the other Sahadeva. Those best of Kurus were born year after year.

sanskrit: kuntīm atha punaḥ pāṇḍur mādryarthe samacodayat tam uvāca pṛthā rājan rahasy uktā satī sadā
english: Then Pāṇḍu urged Kuntī again on Mādrī's behalf. Pṛthā said to him: 'O king, I was told this in private only once.'

sanskrit: uktā sakṛd dvandvam eṣā lebhe tenāsmi vañcitā bibhemy asyāḥ paribhavān nārīṇāṃ gatir īdṛśī
english: 'When spoken to once, she obtained a twin—by that I was deceived. I fear being surpassed by her; such is the way of women.'

sanskrit: nājñāsiṣam ahaṃ mūḍhā dvandvāhvāne phaladvayam tasmān nāhaṃ niyoktavyā tvayaiṣo 'stu varo mama
english: 'Foolish that I was, I did not know that invoking for a pair yields two sons. Therefore I should not be urged by you again—let this be my boon from you.'

sanskrit: evaṃ pāṇḍoḥ sutāḥ pañca devadattā mahābalāḥ saṃbhūtāḥ kīrtimantas te kuruvaṃśavivardhanāḥ
english: Thus the five sons of Pāṇḍu, given by the gods and of great strength, were born—renowned and extenders of the Kuru lineage.

sanskrit: śubhalakṣaṇasaṃpannāḥ somavat priyadarśanāḥ siṃhadarpā maheṣvāsāḥ siṃhavikrāntagāminaḥ siṃhagrīvā manuṣyendrā vavṛdhur devavikramāḥ
english: Endowed with auspicious marks, lovely to behold as the moon, proud as lions, great archers, striding with a lion's valor, lion-necked lords of men—they grew up with godlike might.

sanskrit: vivardhamānās te tatra puṇye haimavate girau vismayaṃ janayām āsur maharṣīṇāṃ sameyuṣām
english: As they grew on that holy Himalayan mountain, they caused wonder among the great seers who gathered there.

sanskrit: te ca pañca śataṃ caiva kuruvaṃśavivardhanāḥ sarve vavṛdhur alpena kālenāpsv iva nīrajāḥ
english: And those five, together with a hundred, who all enlarged the Kuru race, grew in a short time like lotuses in water.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca darśanīyāṃs tataḥ putrān pāṇḍuḥ pañca mahāvane tān paśyan parvate reme svabāhubalapālitān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Pāṇḍu then rejoiced on the mountain in the great forest, beholding his five handsome sons, guarded by the strength of his own arms.

sanskrit: supuṣpitavane kāle kadā cin madhumādhave bhūtasaṃmohane rājā sabhāryo vyacarad vanam
english: Once, in the sweet spring season when the forest was in full bloom and all creatures were bewildered with desire, the king wandered through the forest with his wife.

sanskrit: palāśais tilakais cūtaiś campakaiḥ pāribhadrakaiḥ anyaiś ca bahubhir vṛkṣaiḥ phalapuṣpasamṛddhibhiḥ
english: The forest was rich with palāśa, tilaka, mango, campaka, and pāribhadraka trees, and many other trees laden with fruits and flowers.

sanskrit: jalasthānaiś ca vividhaiḥ padminībhiś ca śobhitam pāṇḍor vanaṃ tu saṃprekṣya prajajñe hṛdi manmathaḥ
english: Adorned with various bodies of water and with lotus ponds, the forest captivated Pāṇḍu's gaze, and desire awakened in his heart.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanasaṃ tatra viharantaṃ yathāmaram taṃ mādry anujagāmaikā vasanaṃ bibhratī śubham
english: As he roamed there with a joyful mind, carefree as an immortal, Mādrī alone followed him, wearing a beautiful garment.

sanskrit: samīkṣamāṇaḥ sa tu tāṃ vayaḥsthāṃ tanuvāsasam tasya kāmaḥ pravavṛdhe gahane 'gnir ivotthitaḥ
english: Beholding her in the fullness of her youth, clad in thin garments, his desire blazed up like fire in a thicket.

sanskrit: rahasy ātmasamāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā rājīvalocanām na śaśāka niyantuṃ taṃ kāmaṃ kāmabalātkṛtaḥ
english: Seeing her lotus-eyed and equal to himself in a secluded place, the king, overpowered by the force of desire, could not restrain that longing.

sanskrit: tata enāṃ balād rājā nijagrāha rahogatām vāryamāṇas tayā devyā visphurantyā yathābalam
english: Then the king forcibly seized her in that solitary place, though the queen struggled and restrained him with all her strength.

sanskrit: sa tu kāmaparītātmā taṃ śāpaṃ nānvabudhyata mādrīṃ maithunadharmeṇa gacchamāno balād iva
english: His soul consumed by desire, he did not recall the curse as he came forcibly upon Mādrī in the act of union.

sanskrit: jīvitāntāya kauravyo manmathasya vaśaṃ gataḥ śāpajaṃ bhayam utsṛjya jagāmaiva balāt priyām
english: The Kaurava, fallen under the sway of Kāma to the end of his life, casting aside the fear born of the curse, came forcibly upon his beloved.

sanskrit: tasya kāmātmano buddhiḥ sākṣāt kālena mohitā saṃpramathyendriyagrāmaṃ pranaṣṭā saha cetasā
english: His intellect, enslaved to desire, was directly deluded by Fate itself; churned by the tumult of the senses, it vanished along with his consciousness.

sanskrit: sa tayā saha saṃgamya bhāryayā kurunandana pāṇḍuḥ paramadharmātmā yuyuje kāladharmaṇā
english: Having united with his wife, O joy of the Kurus, the supremely virtuous Pāṇḍu met with the law of death.

sanskrit: tato mādrī samāliṅgya rājānaṃ gatacetasam mumoca duḥkhajaṃ śabdaṃ punaḥ punar atīva ha
english: Then Mādrī embraced the king, whose consciousness had departed, and cried out again and again in inconsolable grief.

sanskrit: saha putrais tataḥ kuntī mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau ājagmuḥ sahitās tatra yatra rājā tathāgataḥ
english: Then Kuntī, together with her sons and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, all came together to where the king lay thus.

sanskrit: tato mādry abravīd rājann ārtā kuntīm idaṃ vacaḥ ekaiva tvam ihāgaccha tiṣṭhantv atraiva dārakāḥ
english: Then Mādrī, distressed, spoke these words to Kuntī: 'Come here alone; let the children stay right there.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasyās tatraivāvārya dārakān hatāham iti vikruśya sahasopajagāma ha
english: Hearing those words, Kuntī stopped the children right there, and crying out 'I am undone!' she quickly came forward.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuṃ ca mādrīṃ ca śayānau dharaṇītale kuntī śokaparītāṅgī vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
english: Seeing Pāṇḍu and Mādrī lying on the ground, Kuntī's body was seized with grief, and she lamented in deep sorrow.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇo mayā nityaṃ vīraḥ satatam ātmavān kathaṃ tvam abhyatikrāntaḥ śāpaṃ jānan vanaukasaḥ
english: 'O hero, always self-possessed, ever guarded by me—how did you transgress the curse knowingly, you who dwell in the forest?'

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā mādri rakṣitavyo janādhipaḥ sā kathaṃ lobhitavatī vijane tvaṃ narādhipam
english: 'O Mādrī, was it not your duty to protect the lord of men? How did you entice the king of men into a lonely place?'

sanskrit: kathaṃ dīnasya satataṃ tvām āsādya rahogatām taṃ vicintayataḥ śāpaṃ praharṣaḥ samajāyata
english: 'How could delight arise in one who was always afflicted, who had reached you alone in a secluded place, pondering that very curse?'

sanskrit: dhanyā tvam asi bāhlīki matto bhāgyatarā tathā dṛṣṭavaty asi yad vaktraṃ prahṛṣṭasya mahīpateḥ
english: 'You are fortunate, O princess of Bāhlika, more blessed than I; for you have seen the face of the king in his moment of joy.'

sanskrit: mādry uvāca vilobhyamānena mayā vāryamāṇena cāsakṛt ātmā na vārito 'nena satyaṃ diṣṭaṃ cikīrṣuṇā
english: Mādrī said: 'Though I enticed him and though I restrained him repeatedly, he could not be stopped by me. Truly, he wished to fulfill his fate.'

sanskrit: kunty uvāca ahaṃ jyeṣṭhā dharmapatnī jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmaphalaṃ mama avaśyaṃ bhāvino bhāvān mā māṃ mādri nivartaya
english: Kuntī said: 'I am the elder lawful wife; the foremost reward of dharma is mine. What must be shall be—O Mādrī, do not turn me away.'

sanskrit: anveṣyāmīha bhartāram ahaṃ pretavaśaṃ gatam uttiṣṭha tvaṃ visṛjyainam imān rakṣasva dārakān
english: 'I shall follow my husband who has passed into the realm of the dead. Rise, leave him to me, and protect these children.'

sanskrit: mādry uvāca aham evānuyāsyāmi bhartāram apalāyinam na hi tṛptāsmi kāmānāṃ taj jyeṣṭhā anumanyatām
english: Mādrī said: 'I shall follow the husband who did not flee. I am not yet satisfied in my desires—let the elder consent to this.'

sanskrit: māṃ cābhigamya kṣīṇo 'yaṃ kāmād bharatasattamaḥ tam ucchindyām asya kāmaṃ kathaṃ nu yamasādane
english: 'This best of Bhāratas was exhausted coming to me in desire—how could I cut off his desire and leave him unsatisfied in Yama's abode?'

sanskrit: na cāpy ahaṃ vartayantī nirviśeṣaṃ suteṣu te vṛttim ārye cariṣyāmi spṛśed enas tathā hi mām
english: 'Nor could I, O noble lady, treat your sons and mine without distinction; sin would touch me if I were to do so.'

sanskrit: tasmān me sutayoḥ kunti vartitavyaṃ svaputravat māṃ hi kāmayamāno 'yaṃ rājā pretavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: 'Therefore, O Kuntī, you must treat my two sons as your own; for this king who desired me has passed into the realm of the dead.'

sanskrit: rājñaḥ śarīreṇa saha mamāpīdaṃ kalevaram dagdhavyaṃ supraticchannam etad ārye priyaṃ kuru
english: 'Along with the king's body, this body of mine too must be burned, well adorned. O noble one, do me this kindness.'

sanskrit: dārakeṣv apramattā ca bhavethāś ca hitā mama ato 'nyan na prapaśyāmi saṃdeṣṭavyaṃ hi kiṃ cana
english: 'And be vigilant and beneficent toward the children for my sake. I see nothing else that I need entrust to you.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā taṃ citāgnisthaṃ dharmapatnī nararṣabham madrarājātmajā tūrṇam anvārohad yaśasvinī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, that glorious lawful wife, daughter of the Madra king, quickly mounted the funeral pyre beside the bull among men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pāṇḍor avabhṛthaṃ kṛtvā devakalpā maharṣayaḥ tato mantram akurvanta te sametya tapasvinaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After performing the final purificatory rites for Pāṇḍu, the god-like great seers and ascetics assembled and took counsel.

sanskrit: hitvā rājyaṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca sa mahātmā mahātapāḥ asmin sthāne tapas taptuṃ tāpasāñ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: 'That great-souled one of great austerity, abandoning kingdom and realm, came to this place seeking refuge among ascetics to practice tapas.'

sanskrit: sa jātamātrān putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca bhavatām iha pradāyopanidhiṃ rājā pāṇḍuḥ svargam ito gataḥ
english: 'King Pāṇḍu, having entrusted his newborn sons and his wives here to your care as a trust, has departed from this place to heaven.'

sanskrit: te parasparam āmantrya sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ pāṇḍoḥ putrān puraskṛtya nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Taking leave of one another, those devoted to the welfare of all beings, placing Pāṇḍu's sons at their head, resolved to go to the city named for the elephant—Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: udāramanasaḥ siddhā gamane cakrire manaḥ bhīṣmāya pāṇḍavān dātuṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrāya caiva hi
english: Those noble-minded perfected ones set their minds on the journey, intending to deliver the Pāṇḍavas to Bhīṣma and to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tasminn eva kṣaṇe sarve tān ādāya pratasthire pāṇḍor dārāṃś ca putrāṃś ca śarīraṃ caiva tāpasāḥ
english: At that very moment all the ascetics set out, taking with them Pāṇḍu's wives, his sons, and also his body.

sanskrit: sukhinī sā purā bhūtvā satataṃ putravatsalā prapannā dīrgham adhvānaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ tad amanyata
english: She who had once been happy, always tender toward her children, though she had undertaken a long journey, felt it as brief.

sanskrit: sā nadīrgheṇa kālena saṃprāptā kurujāṅgalam vardhamānapuradvāram āsasāda yaśasvinī
english: In no great time that glorious one reached the Kuru countryside and arrived at the gate of the city of Vardhamāna.

sanskrit: taṃ cāraṇasahasrāṇāṃ munīnām āgamaṃ tadā śrutvā nāgapure nṝṇāṃ vismayaḥ samajāyata
english: Hearing of the arrival of thousands of wandering bards and sages at that time, the people of Nāgapura were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: muhūrtodita āditye sarve dharmapuraskṛtāḥ sadārās tāpasān draṣṭuṃ niryayuḥ puravāsinaḥ
english: As the sun rose a short while later, all the city's residents, placing dharma foremost, went out with their wives to see the ascetics.

sanskrit: strīsaṃghāḥ kṣatrasaṃghāś ca yānasaṃghān samāsthitāḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha nirjagmur brāhmaṇānāṃ ca yoṣitaḥ
english: Groups of women and groups of Kṣatriyas mounted on conveyances went out together with Brahmins, and the wives of Brahmins as well.

sanskrit: tathā viṭśūdrasaṃghānāṃ mahān vyatikaro 'bhavat na kaś cid akarod īrṣyām abhavan dharmabuddhayaḥ
english: Likewise there was a great mingling of groups of Vaiśyas and Śūdras; no one acted with jealousy—they all came with minds turned to dharma.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ somadatto 'tha bāhlikaḥ prajñācakṣuś ca rājarṣiḥ kṣattā ca viduraḥ svayam
english: So too Bhīṣma son of Śantanu, and Somadatta, and Bāhlika, the royal sage who sees with the eyes of wisdom, and the charioteer's son Vidura himself.

sanskrit: sā ca satyavatī devī kausalyā ca yaśasvinī rājadāraiḥ parivṛtā gāndhārī ca viniryayau
english: And the goddess Satyavatī, and the glorious Kausalyā, and Gāndhārī surrounded by the royal women—all went out.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dāyādā duryodhanapurogamāḥ bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇaiś citraiḥ śatasaṃkhyā viniryayuḥ
english: The heirs of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, led by Duryodhana, adorned with varied ornaments, went out numbering a hundred.

sanskrit: tān maharṣigaṇān sarvāñ śirobhir abhivādya ca upopaviviśuḥ sarve kauravyāḥ sapurohitāḥ
english: All the Kauravas, bowing their heads in salutation to all those groups of great seers, sat down near them together with their priests.

sanskrit: tathaiva śirasā bhūmāv abhivādya praṇamya ca upopaviviśuḥ sarve paurajānapadā api
english: In the same way all the city folk and country people bowed their heads to the ground in reverence and sat down nearby.

sanskrit: tam akūjam ivājñāya janaughaṃ sarvaśas tadā bhīṣmo rājyaṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca maharṣibhyo nyavedayat
english: Perceiving that multitude of people to be silent, as if mute, Bhīṣma then reported to the great seers the state of the kingdom and the realm.

sanskrit: teṣām atho vṛddhatamaḥ pratyutthāya jaṭājinī maharṣimatam ājñāya maharṣir idam abravīt
english: Then the eldest among them, wearing matted locks and a deerskin, rose up, and discerning the mind of the great seers, that great seer spoke thus.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa kauravyadāyādaḥ pāṇḍur nāma narādhipaḥ kāmabhogān parityajya śataśṛṅgam ito gataḥ
english: 'He who was the Kaurava heir, the lord of men named Pāṇḍu, renouncing pleasures and enjoyments, departed from here to Śataśṛṅga.'

sanskrit: brahmacaryavratasthasya tasya divyena hetunā sākṣād dharmād ayaṃ putras tasya jāto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: 'While he abided in the vow of celibacy, by a divine cause, Yudhiṣṭhira, this son of his, was born directly from Dharma himself.'

sanskrit: tathemaṃ balināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ mātariśvā dadau putraṃ bhīmaṃ nāma mahābalam
english: 'Likewise, to that great-souled king, Mātariśvan—the Wind—gave this son Bhīma by name, foremost of the strong and of great might.'

sanskrit: puruhūtād ayaṃ jajñe kuntyāṃ satyaparākramaḥ yasya kīrtir maheṣvāsān sarvān abhibhaviṣyati
english: 'This one of true valor was born to Kuntī from Indra, the lord of many; his glory will surpass all great archers.'

sanskrit: yau tu mādrī maheṣvāsāv asūta kurusattamau aśvibhyāṃ manujavyāghrāv imau tāv api tiṣṭhataḥ
english: 'And these two great archers, the best of Kurus and tigers among men, whom Mādrī bore from the Aśvins—they too stand here.'

sanskrit: caratā dharmanityena vanavāsaṃ yaśasvinā eṣa paitāmaho vaṃśaḥ pāṇḍunā punar uddhṛtaḥ
english: 'By the glorious Pāṇḍu who dwelt in the forest, ever constant in dharma, this ancestral lineage has been raised up once more.'

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ janma vṛddhiṃ ca vaidikādhyayanāni ca paśyataḥ satataṃ pāṇḍoḥ śaśvat prītir avardhata
english: 'As Pāṇḍu watched the birth, the growth, and the Vedic studies of his sons, his joy grew ever and always.'

sanskrit: vartamānaḥ satāṃ vṛtte putralābham avāpya ca pitṛlokaṃ gataḥ pāṇḍur itaḥ saptadaśe 'hani
english: 'Abiding in the conduct of the good, having attained the gift of sons, Pāṇḍu departed from here to the world of the ancestors on the seventeenth day.'

sanskrit: taṃ citāgatam ājñāya vaiśvānaramukhe hutam praviṣṭā pāvakaṃ mādrī hitvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: 'Learning that he had been placed on the funeral pyre and offered to Vaiśvānara, Mādrī entered the fire, abandoning her own life.'

sanskrit: sā gatā saha tenaiva patilokam anuvratā tasyās tasya ca yat kāryaṃ kriyatāṃ tadanantaram
english: 'She has gone, devoted, to the world of her husband along with him. Let whatever rites are due for them both be performed forthwith.'

sanskrit: ime tayoḥ śarīre dve sutāś ceme tayor varāḥ kriyābhir anugṛhyantāṃ saha mātrā paraṃtapāḥ
english: 'Here are their two bodies, and here are their noble sons, scorchers of foes—let them be honored with the rites together with their mother.'

sanskrit: pretakārye ca nirvṛtte pitṛmedhaṃ mahāyaśāḥ labhatāṃ sarvadharmajñaḥ pāṇḍuḥ kurukulodvahaḥ
english: 'And when the funeral rites are completed, let Pāṇḍu of great glory, the upholder of the Kuru house, who knows all dharma, receive the ancestral offering.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā kurūn sarvān kurūṇām eva paśyatām kṣaṇenāntarhitāḥ sarve cāraṇā guhyakaiḥ saha
english: Having spoken thus to all the Kurus, while the Kurus themselves watched, all the wandering bards together with the Guhyakas vanished in an instant.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraṃ tatraivāntarhitaṃ punaḥ ṛṣisiddhagaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ te paraṃ yayuḥ
english: Seeing that assembly of seers and perfected ones vanish right there like a city of the Gandharvas, they were overcome with supreme wonder.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca pāṇḍor vidura sarvāṇi pretakāryāṇi kāraya rājavad rājasiṃhasya mādryāś caiva viśeṣataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'O Vidura, have all the funeral rites performed for Pāṇḍu in a manner befitting a king, for the lion among kings, and especially for Mādrī as well.'

sanskrit: paśūn vāsāṃsi ratnāni dhanāni vividhāni ca pāṇḍoḥ prayaccha mādryāś ca yebhyo yāvac ca vāñchitam
english: 'Distribute cattle, garments, jewels, and various wealth for Pāṇḍu and Mādrī—to whosoever wishes, as much as they desire.'

sanskrit: yathā ca kuntī satkāraṃ kuryān mādryās tathā kuru yathā na vāyur nādityaḥ paśyetāṃ tāṃ susaṃvṛtām
english: 'Arrange also that Kuntī performs honor to Mādrī's rites; see that she is well-protected so that neither the wind nor the sun may look upon her.'

sanskrit: na śocyaḥ pāṇḍur anaghaḥ praśasyaḥ sa narādhipaḥ yasya pañca sutā vīrā jātāḥ surasutopamāḥ
english: 'Sinless Pāṇḍu is not to be mourned; that lord of men is praiseworthy—five heroic sons equal to sons of the gods have been born to him.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca viduras taṃ tathety uktvā bhīṣmeṇa saha bhārata pāṇḍuṃ saṃskārayām āsa deśe paramasaṃvṛte
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Vidura, having said 'so be it' to him, O Bhārata, together with Bhīṣma, performed the funerary consecration for Pāṇḍu in a most secluded spot.

sanskrit: tatas tu nagarāt tūrṇam ājyahomapuraskṛtāḥ nirhṛtāḥ pāvakā dīptāḥ pāṇḍo rājapurohitaiḥ
english: Then from the city, blazing fires preceded by oblations of clarified butter were swiftly brought out by Pāṇḍu's royal priests.

sanskrit: athainam ārtavair gandhair mālyaiś ca vividhair varaiḥ śibikāṃ samalaṃcakrur vāsasācchādya sarvaśaḥ
english: Then they adorned the bier with seasonal fragrances and various choice garlands, covering it all over with cloth.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā śobhitāṃ mālyair vāsobhiś ca mahādhanaiḥ amātyā jñātayaś caiva suhṛdaś copatasthire
english: The ministers, kinsmen, and friends attended upon that bier thus adorned with garlands and with the most precious garments.
